title: Privacy-Preserving GNN Inference on Financial Transaction Graphs via Homomorphic Encryption
abstract: arXiv:2610.18054v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Anti-money laundering (AML) in financial networks requires modeling transaction patterns that span multiple institutions. In practice, however, banks cannot share account and transaction features due to strict privacy regulations. We propose a privacy-preserving graph neural network (GNN) inference framework tailored to this multi-bank setting. A central server holds the graph connectivity and pretrained model weights in plaintext, while each bank keeps its transaction features encrypted. Inference is then carried out entirely on encrypted features under the CKKS homomorphic encryption scheme, so that no plaintext transaction features or predictions are exposed to the server. The key to making this practical is an edge-centric GNN architecture, wherein message passing is expressed through operations on node--edge incidence matrices. translated_title: 基于同态加密的金融交易图上隐私保护的图神经网络推理
translated_abstract: 金融网络中的反洗钱（AML）需要对跨越多个机构的交易模式进行建模。然而在实践中，由于严格的隐私法规，银行无法共享账户和交易特征。我们提出了一种专为这种多银行场景量身定制的隐私保护图神经网络（GNN）推理框架。中央服务器以明文形式持有图的连接结构和预训练模型权重，而每家银行则将其交易特征加密保存。随后的推理过程在CKKS同态加密方案下完全基于加密特征进行，因此任何明文交易特征或预测结果都不会暴露给服务器。使这一方法切实可行的关键是一种以边为中心的GNN架构，其中消息传递通过节点-边关联矩阵上的运算来表达。这种表述方式不仅保留了交易网络中带边属性的多重图结构……
tldr: 该论文提出了一种基于CKKS同态加密、以边为中心的图神经网络推理框架，使多家银行能够在不共享明文交易特征的前提下协作进行反洗钱检测。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a privacy-preserving GNN inference framework with an edge-centric architecture under CKKS homomorphic encryption, enabling multi-bank anti-money laundering detection without exposing plaintext transaction features.
